text:
Olivia Park: ran an nvprof/nsys sweep after the last runtime change, seeing weird stall when KV cache warms up  
Samir Gupta: ugh ok rough summary? numbers?  
Olivia Park: baseline (before PR #892): tail p95 ~ 42ms, after PR #892 p95 jumped to ~72ms for the 1k token trace; looked like a kernel switch at warmup on long sequences  
Junaid Khan: what profiler did you run? nvprof, nsys, perfetto?  
Olivia Park: started with nvprof to get per-kernel timings, then a focused nsys timeline for the run where the scheduler picks the slow matmul kernel. perfetto for the full-system view.  
Mia Chen: can you paste the nvprof snippet?  
Olivia Park: here (trimmed):
```
== NVPROF: Profiling result 
GPU activities: 
  kernelA (fast_gemm)  32.5%  13.8ms 
  kernelB (kv_apply)   45.2%  19.2ms  <-- dominant during warmup window
  kernelC (slow_gemm)  22.3%  9.5ms  
```
Olivia Park: after PR the selector picks slow_gemm earlier in the timeline, and kv_apply increases due to extra copy for cache reconciliation  
Samir Gupta: do we have the nsys timeline slice? need to see concurrency and CUpti markers  
Olivia Park: dropped a 5s nsys trace, exported flame, attached lines: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt ./bench --model xxx --seq 1024
```
Olivia Park: timeline shows repeated alternating blocks: kv_apply -> kernel_switch -> slow_gemm, instead of kv_apply -> fast_gemm  
Junaid Khan: could be a heuristic regression in kernel_selector: PR #892 changed the cost model to add a 1.1x penalty for tiled kernels when kv occupancy low  
Mia Chen: did bisect narrow to a commit?  
Olivia Park: yeh bisected to commit a7f3b2 (the cost-model tweak). Reproduces locally with: 
```
RUNTIME_CONFIG=\"batch_strategy=adaptive;kv_prefetch=on\" ./runner --warmup 50 --requests 200
```
Olivia Park: nvprof diff (before vs after commit): slow_gemm time doubled during initial 30 iterations, but fast_gemm time unchanged  
Samir Gupta: hypothesis: kv warmup causes smaller effective batch shapes mid-run, cost-model misestimates and picks kernel with worse setup overhead  
Junaid Khan: yeah could be we're not accounting for KV cache priming cost. The selector assumes steady-state sequence length and fails on short-burst variance  
Mia Chen: quick test: can you force selector to pick fast_gemm with env override to confirm perf delta?  
Olivia Park: did that: setting KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fast_gemm gets p95 back to 44ms  
perf-bot: automated test run: kernel_selector regression test triggered for commit a7f3b2, failing 3/3 benchmarks  
Samir Gupta: can we add a micro-test that exercises warmup shapes and verifies selector picks fast_gemm when kv occupancy < 0.2?  
Junaid Khan: plan: revert the 1.1x penalty and add occupancy-aware correction. I'll open a PR with the revert+test. Reference traces and nvprof outputs in the pr.
Mia Chen: also add an nsys smoke job in CI for the warmup scenario so we catch this earlier  
Olivia Park: creating issue and will attach the nsys/profile exports + short perfetto screenshots. thanks all :thumbsup:  
Samir Gupta: nice sleuthing :mag:  
Olivia Park: FYI the full trace is ~1.2GB, uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/3799998000_kv_warmup.nsys
Mia Chen: follow-up: let's add a quick checklist to the PR template: include warmup shapes, nvprof/nsys command line, and env overrides for force-kernel.
Olivia Park: updated the ticket with checklist and next steps.
